issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for Animal: the UML in the problem statement specifies Animal(String, int) (a name and an age), but the solution implements Animal with a single-argument constructor Animal(String). The template's Main also shows creating Seal/Pig/Goat with a single String argument. This inconsistency will confuse students about the required constructor signature for Animal and its subclasses and may prevent them from implementing constructors compatible with the provided example usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the mismatch by choosing one of the two consistent designs: (A) Update the UML/problem text to require Animal(String) (remove age) so subclasses and example usage remain single-argument, or (B) Update the template and solution to implement Animal(String, int), add the age field and corresponding getter/setter, and update all subclass constructors and the Main usage to pass an age argument.

issues.description: Attribute mismatch for Animal: the UML in the problem statement declares an 'age: int' attribute for Animal, but the solution's Animal class only defines a 'name' attribute and omits 'age'. This contradicts the UML and may confuse students about which attributes they must implement and initialize.
issues.suggestedFix: Either add the 'age' field (int) to the Animal class in the solution and template, update the constructor to initialize both name and age, and provide getter/setter for age; or update the UML/problem statement to remove the age attribute so that the textual instructions, example usage, template, and solution all consistently require only the name attribute.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement defines Animal with an attribute 'age' and a constructor Animal(String, int), but the provided template usage and the solution implementation use single-argument constructors (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")) and the Solution's Animal class only declares a 'name' field and Animal(String). This mismatch of the identifier 'age' and the constructor signature can confuse students: they may attempt to implement Animal(String, int) and an 'age' attribute to match the UML, but the template main and solution expect single-argument constructors. The inconsistent presence/absence of the 'age' identifier and differing constructor signatures creates an unnecessary mapping burden between the UML in the problem statement and the code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor and attribute specification consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement UML to remove the 'age' attribute and specify Animal(String) as the constructor (so UML matches the template Main usage and solution), or (B) update the template and solution to include an 'age' field and use Animal(String, int) constructors in Animal and all subclasses (and adjust Main accordingly). Prefer option (A) if the exercises and tests expect single-argument constructors.
